cases.observation: The 11Q5 excerpt is printed without supplied-letter brackets or uncertainty marks in the versioned transcription; no fresh image reading was performed. It has God, not YHWH, and lacks all before words; the Greek and Syriac controls likewise lack all there but use Lord. Syriac has zadiq in the second colon, unlike Hebrew hasid and Greek hosios, and unlike Syriac's own merciful adjective in 145:17. A common line-presence class cannot certify exact Hebrew agreement or independent transmission. The repeated blessing in 11Q5 is a separate unit, not part of the quoted nun line. The existing adjudication pilot tentatively prefers inclusion but leaves exact wording unresolved; this evidence ledger does not itself select a source.

cases.observation: POB 22:16 uniquely aligns by full consonantal verse text with WLC 22:17; Greek control locus is 21:17. The published Nahal Hever consonants differ from WLC and must not be dismissed as merely versional or Christian evidence. Their unpointed spelling does not settle lexical derivation, meaning, or historical priority. 4Q88 has uncertain kaf/resh and a supplied final waw, not another secure complete verb. Preserve the Nahal Hever extra he/uncertainty in the following word and the supplied feet; do not normalize away diplomatic difficulties. The CAL Syriac control has a tearing/piercing action; the Aramaic Targum retains lion imagery with a biting expansion. Each supports only the stated reading in its own language. Neither establishes exact Hebrew retroversion, independence, or priority. No local variant marker is displayed in either excerpt, which does not establish manuscript unanimity. Full DJD material review, later reassessments and versional apparatus work remain open.
